Subject: MAP: evidence windows, DPA sequencing & signature fallback plan

Hi Claire —

Following our call earlier, attached is MAP_Clarion_v3.xlsx (master MAP + evaluation checklist) and a short extract of the DPA items we expect Clarion to prioritize (DPA-extract-comments.pdf). High-level asks:

- Can your procurement team confirm which DPA clauses are absolute blockers for legal sign-off (data residency, audit log access, subprocessors)?
- Do you require the order form to be countersigned by Clarion legal before Redwood can start provisioning, or would procurement accept a pre-signed order form with conditional activation pending DPA?
- Requested evidence: SOC2 summary, sample audit log export (masked), and a short runbook for data deletion requests.

Two proposed close paths (we'll finalize based on your blockers):
1) Fast-track (preferred if procurement agrees): Redwood sends signed OF -> Clarion countersigns OF as conditional activation; DPA signed within 7 business days. We hold an escrow/activation trigger in the OF that allows provisioning only after DPA execution or an agreed workaround.
2) Standard: MSA executed -> DPA executed -> OF countersigned -> provisioning.

Target dates (proposal):
- Clarion to confirm blockers & evidence windows by EOD Fri 4/16
- Redwood legal to produce DPA response/redline by Tue 4/20
- If fast-track accepted: OF routing to Clarion for signature by Wed 4/21; provisioning earliest Mon 4/26 with conditional gating.

Please let me know which path your team prefers and who on procurement/legal will own each item. If helpful I can sketch a short procurement runbook for your ops team.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the MAP and clarity. Quick notes from procurement/legal intake:

- Data residency is a hard requirement (Clarion requires EU-resident staging for PHI processing). If Redwood cannot commit to a residency approach in the DPA, legal will not sign.
- Audit logs: procurement needs a short example export and confirmation of retention windows.
- Subprocessors: we have a short list of disallowed subprocessors — we will send as an attachment tomorrow (we're compiling).

Regarding the order form: procurement prefers the OF countersigned before provisioning. That said, we can consider a pre-signed OF with a conditional activation clause if Redwood's legal can provide a compensating control (e.g., automatic suspension if DPA isn't signed within 10 business days).

I attached a living list of clarion questions (Clarion_questions_0414.docx). I'll confirm who will own the DPA redline by EOD Fri 4/16.

Claire

Laura / Marissa —

Thanks Claire for the intake. Quick legal take and proposed sequencing to keep the MAP tight while addressing Clarion's constraints. Summary below; I'll own the DPA redline and coordinate with Claire's team.

Key constraints from Clarion: data residency (EU staging for PHI), audit log sample + retention, subprocessors blacklist.

Proposed sequencing (two-track approach):

A) Fast-track (conditional activation) — owners and controls
- Step 1 (Day 0): Redwood sends a pre-filled OF (price + PO template), countersign capability on Clarion side retained.
- Step 2 (Day 0–3): Redwood legal sends DPA redline focused on residency and subprocessors; includes compensating controls for provisional activation (e.g., IP ACLs, masking, temporary VM isolation).
- Step 3 (Day 3–10): Clarion countersigns OF with conditional activation clause + accepts short-term compensating controls. If DPA not executed by Day 10, automatic suspension clause triggers; funds settlement deferred.
- Owners: Marcus Lin (Redwood legal), Marissa Cole (CS/customer ops), Claire (Clarion procurement).

B) Standard (sequential sign) — if Clarion cannot accept conditional activation
- Step 1: MSA signature
- Step 2: DPA execution (legal-to-legal redline complete)
- Step 3: OF countersigned -> provisioning window scheduled

Action items (today):
- Claire: send subprocessors blacklist + confirm whether Clarion's legal will redline or request Redwood to propose. (Due: 4/16 EOD)
- Laura / Marissa: prepare short provisioning runbook and SOC2 evidence packet (I can pull the sample audit log export). (Due: 4/19)
- Marcus: produce DPA redline focusing on residency and suspension triggers. (Target: 4/20)

Notes on evidence windows: please consider three levels in the MAP spreadsheet — showstopper (must have before provisioning), gating evidence (required within 10 business days of OF), and post-provision evidence (within 30 days). That aligns with Clarion's risk tolerance.

I'll drop the DPA redline into the shared Drive link once ready.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Claire —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and Marcus for the sequencing. We spoke internally and are aligned to pursue the fast-track conditional-activation path so Clarion can begin limited provisioning earlier while the DPA is finalized. Key confirmations:

- Redwood will provide SOC2 summary + masked audit log export by Mon 4/19 (Marissa to own).
- Marcus will deliver a DPA redline that includes: EU-residency commitment for PHI staging, a subprocessors carve-out process, and an automatic suspension trigger if DPA not finalized within 10 business days of OF countersign (Marcus target 4/20).
- OF will include conditional activation language and payment holdback terms; Clarion must counter-sign the OF for provisioning to start.
